claim: Ikoyi holds two MICHELIN Stars and is listed in the 2026 UK MICHELIN Guide
quote: A creative, West African-influenced Two-MICHELIN-Star restaurant in central London

claim: Akoko holds one MICHELIN Star; ten-course tasting menu inspired by Nigeria, Ghana and Senegal
quote: The kitchen adds a creative spin to recipes from across the region – be it Ghanaian abunuabunu, Senegalese yassa or Nigerian jollof rice

claim: Chishuru holds one MICHELIN Star; listed as a fun and welcoming West African restaurant in Fitzrovia
quote: A fun and welcoming place underpinned by delicious West African cuisine

claim: Akara received a Michelin Bib Gourmand in the 2026 UK Guide for good quality, good value West African cooking
quote: Tucked underneath the arches in Borough Yards; sharp execution and careful balancing of flavours runs throughout

claim: The MICHELIN Guide's own roundup of African restaurants in London features only West African establishments — no North or East African starred venues
quote: The best African restaurants in London

claim: Akara (Borough Yards) was awarded a Bib Gourmand in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide round
quote: From the Akoko team, this West African restaurant has a menu built around deep-fried akaras

claim: Ikoyi (2 stars), Akoko (1 star) and Chishuru (1 star) are all listed among London's 2026 Michelin-starred restaurants
Ikoyi was named Best Global Restaurant in Food & Wine's 2026 Tastemakers Awards, announced 15 April 2026
quote: Ikoyi named Best Global Restaurant in Food & Wine's 2026 Tastemakers Awards

claim: Time Out called Ikoyi 'an otherworldly experience' and confirmed the Food & Wine best-in-world award in April 2026
quote: A meal at Ikoyi is an otherworldly experience. From the flavours (phenomenal) to the cost (astronomical), everything at this intimate, intoxicating restaurant will be carved upon your memory.

claim: Ikoyi's tasting menus are priced at £380 (full) and £170 (shorter); tables release on the 1st of each month at 12:00 GMT, bookable up to 2 months ahead
quote: Reservations released on the 1st of each month at 12:00 pm GMT. Can book up to two months in advance.

claim: Akoko's dinner tasting menu is £130 with optional wine pairing; lunch £65 or £130; open Mon–Sat, closed Sundays; cannot accommodate tomatoes, alliums, ginger, or coconut milk
quote: Allow up to 2.5 hours for the full tasting menu and 1.5 hours for the lunch menu

claim: Chishuru is named from a Hausa phrase meaning 'the silence that descends on the table when the food arrives'; specialises in Yoruba, Igbo and Hausa cuisines
quote: Chishuru is a Hausa phrase meaning the silence that descends on the table when the food arrives

claim: Akara is located at Arch 208, 18 Stoney Street, Borough Yards; open Mon 5–11pm, Tue–Sat 12–11pm, Sun 12–10:30pm
quote: Akara — a blend of the crispy, fluffy attributes of Nigerian Akara Osu with the flavour-packed delights of Brazilian Acaraje

claim: Chishuru's lunch tasting menu is £45; dinner £95; signature dishes include guinea fowl yassa, sinasir rice cake, moi moi, and ekoki corn cake; Chef of the Year 2024 (National Restaurant Awards)
quote: Chef Adejoke Bakare's restaurant earned a Michelin star in 2024 while maintaining an approachable philosophy

claim: Akoko's signature dishes include ox tongue suya with bone marrow, waina fermented rice cake with chicken liver, and monkfish with ayamase green pepper sauce; uses an open charcoal grill
quote: A refined exploration of West African cuisine drawing on the rich culinary traditions of Ghana, Nigeria, and Senegal through innovative tasting menus

claim: Joké Bakare is the first Black woman to earn a Michelin star in the UK, and only the second in the world; Akoko and Chishuru both won stars in the 2024 round
quote: The rise of West African cuisine: Michelin stars for Chishuru and Akoko

claim: Aji Akokomi of Akoko discusses leading the way for West African cooking in London; star awarded for cuisine that proves dishes from Nigeria, Ghana and Senegambia deserve the fine-dining treatment
quote: Akoko won its first MICHELIN Star, and the restaurant introduced refined West African cooking to the British dining scene

claim: Jeremy Chan's Ikoyi builds a spice-based cuisine from British-sourced proteins and produce, layering herbs and spices from across Africa and Asia; the restaurant resists easy categorisation
quote: At Ikoyi, that means a precise use of herbs and spices from across Africa and Asia, layered with techniques drawn from around the world, while sourcing proteins and produce from the British Isles
